velixir volume <sub>      The app's persistent volume (one per app, paid plans)

    show                    Size, usage and snapshot settings (the default)
    create                  Add a volume and redeploy to mount it
      --path, -p <path>       Mount path (default /data)
      --limit, -l <GB>        Size, 1 to 50 (default 10), billed at €0.15/GB a month.
                              Emails at 80% and 90%; at 100% the app stops after 24 hours
      --snapshots, -S <when>  daily (default), weekly or off
      --keep, -k <days>       Keep snapshots 7 (default), 14, 30 or 90 days
      --no-redeploy           Mount it on the next deploy instead
    limit <GB>              Change the limit (alias: resize)
    snapshots               List snapshots
      --frequency, -f <when>  ...or change how often: daily, weekly, off
      --keep, -k <days>       ...and/or how long they're kept
    snapshot                Take a snapshot now
    restore <snapshot>      Replace the volume's contents with a snapshot (--yes to skip the prompt)
    cleanup                 Start an app stopped for being over its limit, for 2 hours, to delete files
    delete                  Delete the volume and its data (--yes to skip the prompt)

  All take --app, -a <id> (default: .velixir.json or VELIXIR_APP_ID).
  A volume app runs one replica; each deploy restarts it, so expect a few seconds of downtime.
  Volumes are capped at 50 GB: warnings at 80% and 90%, the app stops 24 hours after it hits
  50 GB, or at once past 60 GB.

velixir env - environment variables for the current app

Usage:
  velixir env [list]                          List variables (secrets are masked)
  velixir env set KEY=value [KEY=value ...]   Set one or more variables
  velixir env unset KEY [KEY ...]             Remove variables
  velixir env import [file|-]                 Import a .env file (default .env), or stdin with -

Options:
  --secret      Store the values encrypted and masked (set, import)
  --redeploy    Redeploy the app afterwards so running pods get the change
  --app <id>    Target a specific app instead of the linked one

Moving from Heroku:
  heroku config -s -a my-app | velixir env import - --secret
PORT and other variables velixir sets itself are skipped on import.
